name: Fixed-speed wind turbine generator (Type 1)
summary: A wind turbine whose squirrel-cage induction generator connects to the network directly, running at nearly constant speed.
description: This symbol marks a Type 1 wind turbine: a rotor-driven squirrel-cage induction generator whose stator connects to the collector network through a soft starter and a step-up transformer, with no power converter in the main path. Speed varies only by the generator slip, typically one or two per cent, so the turbine is described as fixed-speed.

On a single-line diagram it is usually drawn as a blade or rotor glyph coupled to a generator circle marked for an induction machine, followed by the soft starter, switched capacitor steps for reactive power and the pad-mount or nacelle transformer. Older wind farms and small community turbines are the main places it still appears.

The symbol does not state the reactive demand of the generator, the capacitor step sizes or how the turbine behaves during voltage dips. Those values come from the turbine data sheet and the grid connection study, because an induction generator draws magnetising current from the network rather than supplying it.
readingNotes: Look for shunt capacitor steps beside the generator; they supply the reactive power the induction machine absorbs.
A soft starter or thyristor bypass shown in series is for connection inrush only, not for speed control.
drawingChecklist: State generator rating, voltage and slip range.
Show soft starter and capacitor compensation steps.
Reference the turbine step-up transformer and collector feeder.
distinction: A Type 1 turbine has no converter in the power path; a Type 3 or Type 4 turbine shows a converter that sets speed and reactive output.
